set.body:
THE SEMANTIC CHANNEL HAS NEVER BEEN BACKED BY A REAL EMBEDDING MODEL. Not on WOG, not anywhere.
The owner asked, and the absence he noticed -- NOBODY HAS EVER ASKED HIM FOR AN API KEY -- was the
tell.

MEASURED, exhaustively:

  NO HTTP CLIENT IN THE BUILD. No http4s, sttp, akka-http, requests, okhttp, java.net.http. There is
  no code path by which this repository can reach a remote model.
  NO API-KEY HANDLING ANYWHERE. My first grep appeared to find "cohere" in eight files; every hit was
  the word COHERENCE. There is nothing.
  EXACTLY TWO CONCRETE EMBEDDERS EXIST, both `LocalBaseline`:
      HashedNgramEmbedder -- "hashed character 3-5-grams plus word uni/bigrams, sign-hashed into a
        fixed dimension and L2-normalized", FNV-1a;
      TfIdfEmbedder -- TF-IDF over a fitted vocabulary.
    `CachingEmbedder` is a decorator over those. That is the complete list.
  AND THE WOG BENCH HARD-WIRES ONE: channels.scala:160,
      `EmbedderSemantic.of(HashedNgramEmbedder[Id](dimension, seed), units, nodes)`.

BOTH BASELINES ARE LEXICAL. Hashed n-grams and TF-IDF measure SURFACE OVERLAP. Neither is a
semantic model in any sense a reviewer would accept.

WHY THIS IS SERIOUS, in three escalating steps:

1. `CostTerm.Semantic` CARRIES THE HIGHEST WEIGHT IN THE COST MODEL -- 1.0, against chart 0.5. The
   most heavily weighted term in our alignment is backed by character n-gram hashing.

2. I MISDESCRIBED m1'S WOG RESULT AND AMPLIFIED IT IN THE LETTER. I wrote that the aligner "finds
   semantically apt ones" -- "hit by an arrow" against the node about arrows. IT FOUND A LEXICAL
   OVERLAP ON THE TOKEN "arrow". I called that semantic aptness in a letter to the whole team and
   used it as evidence that the machinery below the floor was sound. The machinery may be sound; the
   evidence I gave for it was a word match.

3. AND IT INVALIDATES THE CALIBRATION PLAN I FILED TWO HOURS AGO. bd-01M19947QTCAYJJYTC003HVDB5 says
   freeze the calibration court BEFORE the corpus arrives so the floor cannot be fitted. Correct, and
   insufficient: CALIBRATING THE EXTERNAL FLOOR AGAINST A LEXICAL PLACEHOLDER WOULD FIT THE CONSTANT
   TO THE WRONG DISTANCE FUNCTION. The floor separates "content cost" from "intrusion". If content
   cost is currently lexical distance, the fitted constant answers a question about word overlap and
   would need discarding the moment a real embedder lands.

WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT, and it is genuinely most of the hard part: the `Embedder[F[_]]` trait, the
space/role/view vocabulary, GeometryId so two configurations never share a space, receipts,
CachingEmbedder, and A PRIVACY GATE THAT ALREADY CONTEMPLATES A REMOTE PROVIDER -- contract.scala
records a decision for "raw sensitive text to remote provider" rather than throwing. THE SEAM EXISTS.
Nothing has been plugged into it.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING: that the baselines are worthless. A deterministic, free, portable, offline
baseline is the right FLOOR to compare against, and having it first is good discipline. The defect is
that IT IS THE ONLY THING WE HAVE, while the model's headline term is named `Semantic`.

REQUIRED, and this reorders the alpha path:
  a real embedding provider behind the existing trait, with its key handled as an OWNER-ONLY
    disposition under Q5's rule -- reachable material we use freely, ANYTHING BEHIND CREDENTIALS THE
    OWNER OBTAINS, and nobody puts a key in this repository;
  a WOG run with baseline versus real embeddings SIDE BY SIDE, because the interesting number is the
    DIFFERENCE, and because that comparison is itself the strongest test of whether the semantic term
    is doing any work;
  the calibration court amended to state which distance function the floor is calibrated AGAINST,
    so a later embedder change invalidates it loudly instead of silently.

OWNER: this is the API key nobody asked you for. Which provider we target is your call and I would
rather ask than assume.
set.title: the Semantic cost term -- highest weight in the model -- has only ever been lexical: no real embedder has ever been connected
